page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is an x86_64 architecture server virtualized via the KVM hypervisor. The system features 16 shared vCPUs paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. The primary hardware accelerator configuration consists of three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 144 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, requiring external network storage solutions for data persistence. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A notable architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation model, which may introduce CPU scheduling latency compared to dedicated core instances, though the system is heavily weighted toward GPU-bound workloads.

Given the high density of Ada Lovelace GPUs and 144 GB of total VRAM, this instance is designed for workloads that bottleneck on GPU memory and parallel processing rather than raw CPU performance. Qualitative cost efficiency is centered on the high GPU-to-CPU ratio, making it suitable for large language model inference, deep learning training, and complex parallel rendering tasks where CPU compute requirements are secondary to GPU acceleration.
